newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bonds, Wall St give Madrid stocks a boost at close.
newsitem.headline: Bonds, Wall St give Madrid stocks a boost at close.

text.p: Madrid stocks overturned huge early losses to close up slightly higher on Friday, helped by gains on Wall Street and in bonds after U.S. jobs data was not as bad as most had expected, dealers said.
The general index rose 0.80 points, 0.23 percent, to 349.16 and the Ibex-35 added 9.74 points, 0.25 percent, to 3,963.07.
Sentiment also bucked up after nerves this week regarding the possible end to favourable tariff changes in sectors such as energy.
Repsol added 55 pesetas to 4,110, while Gas Natural added 350 pesetas to 20,390.

Endesa, which hit a low of 7,040 earlier, added 50 pesetas to 7,240. But doubts over the removal of an advantageous government stance towards the firm, along with bigger questions overhanging the sector will likely resurge, and trading could be erratic, dealers said.
Santander, still benefitting from broker recommendations and some switching out of utilities, rose 110 pesetas to 6,420.
In all the outlook remains determined by clues on the 1997 budget, dealers said, and trade could be jumpy until the end of the month.
